changes: notes: added that the year could be 1557 or 1558 CE depending on the reckoning, and noted the catalogue's variant scribe name 'Śrīgiviṃda'

notes: 'saṃ. 1615' in a Devanagari manuscript is taken as Vikrama Saṃvat. If the year is Caitrādi, Kārttika kṛṣṇa 8 of VS 1615 falls in Oct/Nov 1558 CE; if it is Kārttikādi, it falls in Oct/Nov 1557 CE. 'kā. Va.' is read as kārttika vadi (dark fortnight), and 'bhaumayuktāyā' gives Tuesday. Uduṃvara (= Audumbara) is probably the scribe's community, lineage or family name (possibly the Audumbara brahmin group) rather than a personal name. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Uduṃvara Śrīgiviṃda', but the colophon reads 'goviṃdena', so Govinda is the right reading. A lacuna (dots) after 'ālekhi' may have held more names or details.
